section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Musical Pulse
section_1.content: Introduce the fundamental tension: You cannot have a note that is both infinitely short in time (a sharp click) and perfectly precise in pitch (a pure frequency).
section_1.example: Visualizing a drum beat (short time, wide range of frequencies) vs. a long flute note (long time, precise frequency).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Fourier Bridge
section_2.content: Briefly explain the Fourier Transform as a prism: it maps a signal from the Time Domain (where it happens) to the Frequency Domain (what it's made of).
section_2.example: An animation showing a complex waveform being decomposed into its constituent sine waves, like a light beam hitting a prism.

section_3.title: The Gaussian Core: The Optimal Compromise
section_3.content: Explain that the Gaussian function is the unique mathematical bridge. It is the 'most compact' function in both domains. As the Gaussian narrows in time, its Fourier Transform broadens in frequency.
section_3.example: A 'breathing' animation of a Gaussian curve narrowing; as it gets skinny, its Fourier counterpart grows wide and flat, illustrating the trade-off.

section_4.title: Formalizing Uncertainty
section_4.content: Present the mathematical inequality: Δt · Δf ≥ 1/(4π). Explain that the product of the widths (spreads) of the two domains is constrained by a constant.
section_4.example: A 'seesaw' balance scale graphic where 'Time Resolution' sits on one side and 'Frequency Resolution' on the other; the fulcrum represents the constant limit.

section_5.title: Application: The Bat's Echolocation
section_5.content: Apply the principle to a real-world scenario. A bat needs to locate prey (needs short pulses) but also identify the prey (needs frequency information). The Uncertainty Principle dictates the bat's pulse design.
section_5.example: A bat emitting a 'chirp'. Show the spectrogram: a short, wide-band signal allows for accurate distance timing, while the 'sweep' captures target-specific acoustic signatures.

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Fourier Bridge", [
            "Fourier transform maps time to frequency.",
            "Signals decompose into constituent sine waves.",
            "Think of it like a prism."

        time_signal = FunctionGraph(lambda t: np.sin(2 * np.pi * t) + 0.5 * np.sin(5 * np.pi * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color=BLUE)

        self.place_at_grid(freq_spectrum, 'D2', 1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(time_signal.copy(), freq_spectrum))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'F3', 0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bats use chirps for echolocation.",
            "Short duration provides distance resolution.",
            "Frequency sweep captures target signature."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Bat's Echolocation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        bat = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bat.svg")
        insect = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/insect.svg")
        
        self.place_at_grid(bat, 'B2', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(insect, 'D5', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(bat, insect)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5 * np.sin(10 * t) * np.exp(-2 * (t - 0.5)**2), 0]),

            color="#FF5733"
        )

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        self.play(wave.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(reflection))
        self.play(reflection.animate.shift(LEFT * 2.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        line = Line(start=bat.get_center(), end=insect.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        delta_t = Text("Δt", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(delta_t, 'D4', 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(line), Write(delta_t))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)
